title: Overview
text: export const metadata = { title: 'Expo SDK 58 guide' }; Expo SDK 58 guide expo-draw-over-apps is an Android-only Expo module for permission-aware, application-owned floating windows. This guide has one supported path: Expo SDK 58, React Native 0.88, and the Expo Modules 2 bridge.

title: Install
text: Install Use Expo's installer so the native window dependencies match your SDK: bash npx expo install expo-draw-over-apps @expo/ui react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets Or with Bun: bash bunx expo install expo-draw-over-apps @expo/ui react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets The module major follows the Expo SDK major, so 58.x is the supported line for SDK 58. Its package metadata requires the expo peer range ^58.0.0 . Because this package contains native Android code, build a development client. It does not run in Expo Go. bash npx expo run:android

title: Choose a window
text: Choose a window Use ReactNativeWindow when the renderer is ordinary React Native UI. It animates width, height, and corner-radius changes with Reanimated. Use NativeWindow when the renderer is Expo UI Jetpack Compose. It is a direct Host , so its children must come from @expo/ui/jetpack-compose , not React Native. API Content Best for ReactNativeWindow React Native views Existing RN components, NativeWind, animated resizing NativeWindow Expo UI Jetpack Compose views Native Material surfaces and Compose modifiers

title: Show it
text: Show it Register a renderer before starting the overlay service, then pass a stable bubble ID. Use physical-pixel x and y coordinates for exact placement or location for one of nine predefined screen positions. tsx import { useEffect } from 'react'; import { closeBubble, setBubbleRendererForBubble, showBubble, } from 'expo-draw-over-apps'; import { StatusWindow } from './StatusWindow'; const BUBBLE_ID = 'status-window'; export function OverlayRegistration() { useEffect(() => { setBubbleRendererForBubble(BUBBLE_ID, StatusWindow); return () => { closeBubble(BUBBLE_ID); setBubbleRendererForBubble(BUBBLE_ID, null); }; }, []); return null; } await showBubble(BUBBLE_ID, { x: 48, y: 180 }); await showBubble(BUBBLE_ID, { location: 'bottom-right' }); Continue with [overlay permission](./permission/), then choose the [React Native window](./react-native-window/) or [native window](./native-window/) tutorial.

title: Multiple windows
text: Multiple windows Need two or more overlays at the same time? The [multiple-window setup guide](./multiple-windows/) has visible tabs for Expo Router and App.tsx / no Router projects, plus examples for independent positions and shared renderers.

title: Permission
text: export const metadata = { title: 'Overlay permission' }; Overlay permission Android requires the user to grant “display over other apps” access before a floating window can be attached.

title: Request permission
text: Request permission Check synchronously, request asynchronously, and only show a window after access is granted. tsx import { useState } from 'react'; import { Button, Text, View } from 'react-native'; import { canDrawOverlays, requestPermission, showBubble, } from 'expo-draw-over-apps'; export function PermissionGate() { const [granted, setGranted] = useState(() => canDrawOverlays()); async function enableOverlays() { await requestPermission(); setGranted(canDrawOverlays()); } return ( {granted ? 'Ready' : 'Permission required'} void enableOverlays()} /> void showBubble('status-window', { x: 48, y: 180 })} /> ); } requestPermission() opens Android system settings when access is missing. The returned value is useful, but checking again after the app resumes is the most reliable source of truth.

title: Refresh on resume
text: Refresh on resume The user leaves your app to change the setting. Refresh when React Native reports that the app is active again. tsx useEffect(() => { const subscription = AppState.addEventListener('change', (state) => { if (state === 'active') { setGranted(canDrawOverlays()); } }); return () => subscription.remove(); }, []); Do not repeatedly reopen settings after a denial. Keep the user in control and explain why your feature needs an overlay.

title: React Native window
text: export const metadata = { title: 'React Native window' }; React Native window ReactNativeWindow is a Reanimated surface for renderers made from React Native views. Your application owns the contents, behavior, dimensions, and cleanup.

title: Complete renderer
text: Complete renderer tsx import { Pressable, StyleSheet, Text } from 'react-native'; import { ReactNativeWindow, showBubble, type BubbleRendererProps, } from 'expo-draw-over-apps'; export function StatusWindow({ bubbleId, close }: BubbleRendererProps) { return ( Upload complete void showBubble(bubbleId, { x: 240, y: 120 })}> Move Close ); } const styles = StyleSheet.create({ window: { borderWidth: 1, borderColor: ' 38bdf8', padding: 16 }, content: { flex: 1, justifyContent: 'space-between' }, title: { color: ' f8fafc', fontSize: 18, fontWeight: '800' }, action: { color: ' 7dd3fc', fontWeight: '700' }, }); The component accepts normal View props plus width , height , borderRadius , backgroundColor , contentContainerStyle , and animationConfig . Set duration: 0 when an immediate resize is preferable.

title: Register and show
text: Register and show tsx import { useEffect } from 'react'; import { closeBubble, setBubbleRendererForBubble, showBubble, } from 'expo-draw-over-apps'; import { StatusWindow } from './StatusWindow'; const BUBBLE_ID = 'status-window'; export function StatusWindowRegistration() { useEffect(() => { setBubbleRendererForBubble(BUBBLE_ID, StatusWindow); return () => { closeBubble(BUBBLE_ID); setBubbleRendererForBubble(BUBBLE_ID, null); }; }, []); return null; } export function showStatusWindow() { return showBubble(BUBBLE_ID, { x: 48, y: 180 }); } Keep the registration mounted while the overlay may be visible. Clearing it with null prevents stale renderer references during fast refresh and navigation changes.

title: Native window
text: export const metadata = { title: 'Native window' }; Native window NativeWindow is a direct Expo UI Jetpack Compose Host . Use it when the overlay content should be a native Compose hierarchy. > Expo UI for Android is beta in Expo SDK 58. Pin SDK-compatible versions and verify behavior on the Android versions you support.

title: Complete renderer
text: Complete renderer tsx import { Button, Column, Shape, Surface, Text } from '@expo/ui/jetpack-compose'; import { fillMaxWidth, paddingAll, size } from '@expo/ui/jetpack-compose/modifiers'; import { NativeWindow, showBubble, type BubbleRendererProps, } from 'expo-draw-over-apps'; export function NativeStatusWindow({ bubbleId, close }: BubbleRendererProps) { return ( Upload complete void showBubble(bubbleId, { x: 240, y: 120 })}> Move Close ); } The exact SDK 58 component and modifier APIs are documented in the [official Expo UI Jetpack Compose reference](https://docs.expo.dev/versions/v58.0.0/sdk/ui/jetpack-compose/).

title: Register and show
text: Register and show Registration is the same for either window type—the renderer component determines which surface is created. tsx import { useEffect } from 'react'; import { closeBubble, setBubbleRendererForBubble, showBubble, } from 'expo-draw-over-apps'; import { NativeStatusWindow } from './NativeStatusWindow'; const BUBBLE_ID = 'native-status-window'; export function NativeStatusRegistration() { useEffect(() => { setBubbleRendererForBubble(BUBBLE_ID, NativeStatusWindow); return () => { closeBubble(BUBBLE_ID); setBubbleRendererForBubble(BUBBLE_ID, null); }; }, []); return null; } export function showNativeStatusWindow() { return showBubble(BUBBLE_ID, { x: 48, y: 180 }); } Do not place React Native View , Text , or Pressable components inside NativeWindow . Use Expo UI Compose components and modifiers throughout that host.

title: Multiple windows
text: import { SetupTab, SetupTabs } from '../../../components/SetupTabs'; export const metadata = { title: 'Multiple overlay windows' }; Multiple overlay windows Every simultaneous window needs a unique, stable ID. Register one renderer for each ID, keep those registrations mounted, then call showBubble once for every window you want to display. The renderer registration and overlay actions are the same in every Expo project. Only the place where you mount the registration differs: - Expo Router: wrap the navigator in the root src/app/_layout.tsx . - Without Expo Router: wrap the existing application UI or navigator in App.tsx .

title: Choose your project setup
text: Choose your project setup Select the project type first, then create the shared registration and action files shown below the tabs. Mount in the root layout Expo Router uses its root _layout.tsx for initialization and top-level providers. Wrap the existing Stack , Tabs , NativeTabs , or other navigator with the registration component. This keeps the renderers registered while users navigate between routes. See Expo's [root layout documentation](https://docs.expo.dev/router/basics/navigation-layouts/ root-layout). tsx // src/app/_layout.tsx import { Stack } from 'expo-router/stack'; import { OverlayWindowsRegistration } from '../overlays/overlay-registration'; export default function RootLayout() { return ( ); } Render the shared controls from any route: tsx // src/app/index.tsx import { OverlayControls } from '../components/overlay-controls'; export default function HomeRoute() { return ; } Projects using a root-level app folder instead of src/app use the same layout code with adjusted relative imports. Mount in App.tsx Wrap the UI already returned by App.tsx . This example renders the shared controls directly: tsx // App.tsx import { OverlayControls } from './src/components/overlay-controls'; import { OverlayWindowsRegistration } from './src/overlays/overlay-registration'; export default function App() { return ( ); } If the project uses React Navigation or another navigator, replace OverlayControls above with that existing navigator. Keep OverlayWindowsRegistration above it so every screen can control the windows. Keep the shared overlay code outside the route directory: text src/ components/ overlay-controls.tsx overlays/ overlay-ids.ts overlay-registration.tsx overlay-actions.ts CallControlsWindow.tsx UploadStatusWindow.tsx

title: Register two renderers
text: Register two renderers Start with constants for the two overlay IDs: tsx // src/overlays/overlay-ids.ts export const CALL_CONTROLS_ID = 'call-controls'; export const UPLOAD_STATUS_ID = 'upload-status'; Create one registration component. This example registers a React Native call controller and a native Compose upload status window. Build those renderer components using the [React Native window](../react-native-window/) and [native window](../native-window/) guides. tsx // src/overlays/overlay-registration.tsx import { useEffect, type PropsWithChildren } from 'react'; import { closeBubble, setBubbleRendererForBubble, } from 'expo-draw-over-apps'; import { CallControlsWindow } from './CallControlsWindow'; import { UploadStatusWindow } from './UploadStatusWindow'; import { CALL_CONTROLS_ID, UPLOAD_STATUS_ID } from './overlay-ids'; export function OverlayWindowsRegistration({ children }: PropsWithChildren) { useEffect(() => { setBubbleRendererForBubble(CALL_CONTROLS_ID, CallControlsWindow); setBubbleRendererForBubble(UPLOAD_STATUS_ID, UploadStatusWindow); return () => { closeBubble(CALL_CONTROLS_ID); closeBubble(UPLOAD_STATUS_ID); setBubbleRendererForBubble(CALL_CONTROLS_ID, null); setBubbleRendererForBubble(UPLOAD_STATUS_ID, null); }; }, []); return children; }

title: Show and control the windows
text: Show and control the windows Create shared actions that work in both project types. Request [Android overlay permission](../permission/) before calling showOverlayWindows . tsx // src/overlays/overlay-actions.ts import { closeBubble, showBubble } from 'expo-draw-over-apps'; import { CALL_CONTROLS_ID, UPLOAD_STATUS_ID } from './overlay-ids'; export async function showOverlayWindows() { const results = await Promise.all([ showBubble(CALL_CONTROLS_ID, { location: 'top-left' }), showBubble(UPLOAD_STATUS_ID, { location: 'bottom-right' }), ]); return results.every(Boolean); } export function closeUploadStatusWindow() { return closeBubble(UPLOAD_STATUS_ID); } The same controls component can be rendered by an Expo Router route, App.tsx , or any screen in an existing navigator: tsx // src/components/overlay-controls.tsx import { Pressable, ScrollView, Text } from 'react-native'; import { closeUploadStatusWindow, showOverlayWindows, } from '../overlays/overlay-actions'; export function OverlayControls() { return ( void showOverlayWindows()}> Show both overlay windows Close only the upload window ); } Calling showBubble again with one ID only repositions that window. Closing one ID does not affect the other registered windows. tsx await showBubble(CALL_CONTROLS_ID, { x: 48, y: 180 }); closeBubble(UPLOAD_STATUS_ID); Add more windows by repeating the same pair: register a unique ID with setBubbleRendererForBubble , then call showBubble with that ID.

title: Reuse one renderer
text: Reuse one renderer Several IDs may share the same renderer. Its BubbleRendererProps include the current bubbleId , so it can read and update the correct window's state. tsx const CONTACT_WINDOW_IDS = ['contact-alex', 'contact-sam', 'contact-lee'] as const; useEffect(() => { for (const bubbleId of CONTACT_WINDOW_IDS) { setBubbleRendererForBubble(bubbleId, ContactWindow); } return () => { for (const bubbleId of CONTACT_WINDOW_IDS) { closeBubble(bubbleId); setBubbleRendererForBubble(bubbleId, null); } }; }, []); await Promise.all( CONTACT_WINDOW_IDS.map((bubbleId, index) => showBubble(bubbleId, { x: 32 + index 72, y: 120 + index 96 }) ) ); Do not reuse one ID for two simultaneous windows. An ID identifies one native overlay surface, so a later call with the same ID updates the existing window instead of creating another one.

title: Window controls
text: export const metadata = { title: 'Window controls' }; Window controls Named windows can be positioned, moved, edge-hidden, inspected, and closed independently.

title: Predefined locations
text: Predefined locations Use location when the window should snap to one of nine screen positions while remaining completely visible. tsx await showBubble('player', { location: 'top-left' }); await showBubble('player', { location: 'top-center' }); await showBubble('player', { location: 'top-right' }); await showBubble('player', { location: 'center-left' }); await showBubble('player', { location: 'center' }); await showBubble('player', { location: 'center-right' }); await showBubble('player', { location: 'bottom-left' }); await showBubble('player', { location: 'bottom-center' }); await showBubble('player', { location: 'bottom-right' }); top and bottom are shorter aliases for top-center and bottom-center . An explicit coordinate overrides the matching preset axis. This keeps the preset's other axis: tsx await showBubble('player', { location: 'bottom-left', x: 120 });

title: Coordinates
text: Coordinates x and y are optional physical screen pixels measured from the display's top-left corner. You may provide either axis independently. tsx await showBubble('player', { x: 48, y: 180 }); await showBubble('player', { x: 240 }); await showBubble('player', { y: 120 }); Android clamps supplied coordinates to the available display bounds so the window remains reachable. Omitting coordinates and location preserves the module's existing placement behavior.

title: Move an open window
text: Move an open window Calling showBubble for an already-visible ID repositions that window immediately. This makes in-window “move” actions straightforward: tsx void showBubble(bubbleId, { x: 240, y: 120 })}> Move window An explicit position also clears an edge-docked offset before applying the new coordinates.

title: Close and edge hide
text: Close and edge hide tsx import { closeAllBubbles, closeBubble, isBubbleVisible, setEdgeHideEnabled, showBubble, } from 'expo-draw-over-apps'; setEdgeHideEnabled(true, 'player'); await showBubble('player', { edgeHideEnabled: true, x: 48, y: 180 }); if (isBubbleVisible('player')) { closeBubble('player'); } closeAllBubbles(); Closing releases the native overlay surface and its React root. Prefer closeBubble over the deprecated hideBubble compatibility alias.

title: Limitations
text: export const metadata = { title: 'Limitations' }; Limitations The module targets Android and requires native code. Plan around these platform constraints before shipping. - Expo Go is not supported; use a development build or a release build. - The user must explicitly grant Android's draw-over-apps permission. - iOS does not offer a general equivalent to Android application overlays. - Expo UI Jetpack Compose is beta in Expo SDK 58. - Overlay coordinates use physical screen pixels, not React Native density-independent layout units. - Android may stop background services under device-specific battery or memory policies. - A floating window can cover content in other apps; use conservative sizes and always provide a clear close action. - Renderer registration lives in JavaScript. Keep the application process and the registration lifecycle in mind when recovering after termination.

title: Production checklist
text: Production checklist 1. Explain the feature before opening Android settings. 2. Provide a visible close action inside every renderer. 3. Test coordinate clamping, dragging, edge hide, rotation, and display cutouts. 4. Test app backgrounding, force-stop, reboot, and OEM battery restrictions. 5. Avoid sensitive content in overlays and overlay shared-value keys. 6. Verify both light and dark themes for ReactNativeWindow and the Compose theme used by NativeWindow . The included example app is the reference for Expo SDK 58. It contains exactly two renderer fixtures—one for each window API—and explicit move actions for emulator testing.
